The bar is short and slim: end to end it is 0.6 of the sailor ring's outside diameter (about 13 mm against the 22 mm ring), never longer than 0.7 of it; it is about half as thick as the ring's tube; its 9 tiny clear stones fill it from tip to tip in one row, with no plain, textured, engraved or stippled block at either end; its one jump ring is at its outer tip. Seen from above, the bar lies across the ring's upper-left tube and its inner tip stops just short of the ring's centre. On the ring, the spring gate is a thinner tube across the top, running from the main tube's flat cut end at 11 o'clock to a short barrel collar at 1 o'clock; the chain's one plain round jump ring hangs on that barrel collar, with no other fittings; the push-pin nub is a small ball on a short stem at 3 o'clock, no wider than a third of the tube; two fine ribbed grooves circle the tube at 4 o'clock, just below the nub. Last time this went wrong, so correct it: the bar grew to 0.87 of the ring, too thick, with oversized stones and an invented stone-less end block; the gate was drawn at full tube thickness and the nub was oversized and fused into a wide ribbed band; the ring sat too low and too far right; the painted gate stood more than twice the ring's height; and the dunes under the chain were brighter than the metal. Every link, the sailor ring, the bar and both jump rings are the same polished 18k gold tone, never silver tone, white metal or rose. Exactly two chain ends in the picture: the long strand that forms the road ends at the ring's barrel collar on one jump ring; a second short strand ends at the bar's one jump ring and runs off the right edge just above the gate; no third strand, no loose jump ring, no extra chain end. LAID AS A ROAD: the chain enters at the left edge and winds in one gentle S across the middle to the right, where the sailor ring lies flat, gate collar and nub visible, the bar across it; the ring is about 19% of the frame width, its centre 41% of the way down the frame and 62% across, and its right edge, nub included, at least 14% of the frame width from the right edge, every link separate. The dunes the chain crosses are a deep dusky ochre-terracotta in soft shadow, darker than the metal, so every link's bright kicker edge is the lightest, most saturated thing on the page; the paler saffron dunes stay behind the procession. No riders, mahouts, drummers or people of any kind on or beside the animals, no water. CONTACT: a fine real shadow under every link, the bar and the ring, with a thin dark contact line wherever the metal touches the paper.
